title: Paediatric dehydration
description: A mother brings her 14-month-old son, who has vomiting and diarrhoea and is difficult to wake.

speaker.name: Lerato Dlamini
speaker.role: the mother and caregiver of the patient
speaker.style: Worried, cooperative, and tired. She sometimes uses home remedies and may not understand medical terms. She becomes tearful when describing how sleepy her child is.

patient.name: Tshepo Dlamini
patient.living_situation: Lives with his mother, father, and older sibling

presenting_complaint: Two days of diarrhoea and vomiting, poor drinking, very few wet nappies, and unusual sleepiness.
opening_line: Sister, Tshepo has been vomiting and having diarrhoea since yesterday. He is very sleepy and has not made a wet nappy since last night.
personality: Worried and protective. She answers questions carefully and appreciates clear explanations. She may minimise how little he has been drinking if she feels judged.

history.onset: Watery diarrhoea started two days ago. Vomiting started yesterday and has become more frequent.
history.stools: Six to eight watery stools today. No blood or mucus in the stool.
history.vomiting: About five episodes since this morning. He cannot keep water or breast milk down.
history.feeding: Breastfeeding much less than usual. He refuses food and has not drunk from a cup today.
history.urine_output: No wet nappy for more than ten hours. The last nappy was only slightly wet.
history.hydration_signs: His eyes look sunken to his mother, he has no tears when crying, and his mouth looks dry.
history.alertness: He is unusually sleepy and floppy. He wakes briefly when spoken to but goes back to sleep.
history.fever: He felt hot at home. The mother thinks his temperature was 38.4 degrees Celsius.
history.past_medical_history: Born at term. No chronic illness. No previous hospital admissions.
history.medications: No chronic medication. The mother gave a little paracetamol yesterday.
history.social_history: Lives in a rural village with both parents and an older sibling. The older sibling had a similar illness last week. The family has limited transport to the clinic.
history.weight: His mother thinks he last weighed about 9 kilograms.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Moderate dehydration due to acute gastroenteritis
red_flags: reduced urine output for more than eight hours
expected_actions: assess airway, breathing, circulation, and level of consciousness
weigh the child and check vital signs, capillary refill, and glucose if available
classify dehydration using a recognised paediatric protocol such as WHO or IMCI
start oral rehydration solution, nasogastric fluids, or intravenous fluids according to severity and local protocol
urgently refer or admit a child with severe dehydration or warning signs
continue breastfeeding and add zinc according to local guidance
avoid anti-diarrhoeal medicines and avoid giving plain water only
give clear safety-netting advice and arrange follow-up

learning_objectives: Assess a child for dehydration using a structured approach
Recognise danger signs in a lethargic child
Choose an appropriate rehydration and referral plan
Communicate clearly with a worried caregiver and check understanding
